result.summary: Do not dispatch as written: the prescribed shutdown wiring misses the pidfile-failure path.

findings.title: Pidfile failures bypass the proposed shutdown call
findings.body: The spec claims the existing finally covers pidfile failures, but src/cli/dream.js handles and throws those failures at lines 414–445, before the try begins at line 461. Applying the two prescribed edits in memory and simulating a failed pidfile write with unsuccessful reaping produced shutdownCalls=0. Output buffered during reaping can therefore be lost when the caller closes the log at line 958; a surviving child's later end handler can flush into that closed stream and trigger an unhandled error. AC2a's direct spawnBrain shutdown test does not exercise this missing caller path.
findings.recommendation: Expand the permitted dream.js edits so shutdown runs in a finally enclosing every post-spawn path, including pidfile creation and its failure reaping. Add a caller-level regression with a failed pidfile write, surviving child, and buffered output; update the two-edit restriction and verification gate accordingly.

next_steps: Correct shutdown scope and add the pidfile-failure regression before closing the design gate.
